purpose: Regression baseline for the ADR constitution, re-run on significant model or harness releases. Not a skill-creator evals.json — skills/adr is retired, so there is no skill_name to match and no with-skill/without-skill toggle; the comparison here is the constitution in project context against an agent working from nothing. Earlier runs of these same prompts are in adr-workspace/iteration-1 and adr-workspace/iteration-2.

evals.prompt: We just decided to use PostgreSQL as our primary database instead of MongoDB for our new SaaS product. We picked Postgres because the team knows it well, it gives us ACID transactions which we need for billing, and it's cheaper to run on AWS RDS than MongoDB Atlas. MongoDB was tempting for its flexible schema but we figured we'd rather have schema discipline. Write an ADR for this.
evals.expected_output: An ADR file at docs/adrs/0001-use-postgresql.md whose frontmatter carries adr and status and nothing else, with a Motivation section explaining why the decision was needed, a Decision Drivers section listing team familiarity/ACID/cost/schema discipline as specific criteria, an Options section comparing PostgreSQL and MongoDB with pros and cons labelled by those exact driver names, a Decision section stating PostgreSQL was chosen and which drivers tipped it, a Consequences section with both good and bad outcomes, and docs/adrs/README.md updated with the new row.

evals.prompt: We need to decide how to handle background jobs in our Rails app. We've been using Sidekiq with Redis but our ops team hates managing Redis and we're looking at switching to GoodJob (which uses Postgres) or Que (also Postgres-backed). GoodJob has a nice UI and active maintenance, Que is simpler but less actively developed. Our main drivers are: ops simplicity (no extra infra), reliability, and team familiarity with Postgres. We're leaning toward GoodJob. Write the ADR.
evals.expected_output: An ADR at docs/adrs/NNNN-use-goodjob-for-background-jobs.md whose filename names the decision rather than the problem, with frontmatter carrying adr and status only, Motivation (ops pain with Redis), Decision Drivers (ops simplicity, reliability, team Postgres familiarity), Options with Sidekiq/Redis, GoodJob, and Que each carrying pros and cons labelled by those exact driver names, Decision choosing GoodJob with rationale, Consequences noting good (no Redis) and bad (Postgres load), README index updated.

evals.prompt: I want to document the decision to go with a monorepo structure for our new platform. We considered a polyrepo approach and a monorepo using Turborepo. Key drivers were: developer experience (easy to make cross-package changes), CI speed, and how easy it is to onboard new engineers. We went with Turborepo monorepo because cross-package refactors are way easier and new engineers only need to clone one repo. Downside is CI caching is more complex and the repo will grow large over time.
evals.expected_output: An ADR at docs/adrs/NNNN-use-turborepo-monorepo.md with frontmatter carrying adr and status only, Motivation (challenges of cross-package changes with polyrepo), Decision Drivers (DX, CI speed, onboarding), Options comparing polyrepo and Turborepo monorepo with pros and cons labelled by those exact driver names, Decision choosing Turborepo, Consequences listing the pros (easy cross-package refactors, single clone) and cons (CI complexity, repo growth), README updated.
